[F001] Side-effect commands actually invoked:

```
$ python3 scripts/sanitization_check.py
$ grep -A1 '^permissions:' .github/workflows/ci.yml
$ grep -E '^## (Reporting a Vulnerability|Supported Versions|Response Timeline)' SECURITY.md
$ JARVIS_SECRETS_DIR=<tmp> python3 scripts/jarvis_doctor.py --skip-auth
$ PYTHONPATH=scripts python3 -m pytest scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/ -q
$ ruff check scripts/sanitization_check.py scripts/jarvis_doctor.py scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_f001_secret_shapes.py
$ ruff format scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_f001_secret_shapes.py
```

## Summary

Implemented F001 baseline hardening in four parts: (a) `scripts/sanitization_check.py` gained the eight enumerated secret-shape regexes (AWS access key, GitHub PAT, GitHub fine-grained tokens, Anthropic, OpenAI, Slack, PEM private-key, JWT) — each with a `# source:` citation per D005 — wired into `scan_line()` so leaks are reported alongside campaign-ID matches; (b) `.github/workflows/ci.yml` got a workflow-root `permissions: contents: read` block with a comment explaining the pwn-request risk; (c) `SECURITY.md` was created at repo root with the required `## Reporting a Vulnerability`, `## Supported Versions`, and `## Response Timeline` sections plus a security-tooling note that explicitly disclaims SAST coverage; (d) `scripts/jarvis_doctor.py` gained `check_sa_key_age()` driven by `JARVIS_SECRETS_DIR` (defaulting to `~/.jarvis/.secrets/`) and a new `warn`-flavored `CheckResult` so age-stale
